title: Filenode -19: access control + subtree change reporting
description: Post-0.5.0 (additive/backend-internal) unless files_rights trait must change. -19 §3.2.3/§5: rename/move/delete check node's own rights; move needs mayAddChildren on new parent; role Directories cannot be destroyed/renamed/moved (forbidden); top-level create without permission forbidden; deleting undiscoverable nodes forbidden; onExists checks rights first. §3.2.2/§5: shareWith change reported on whole subtree, newly undiscoverable nodes reported destroyed. §3.1.1/§9.2 rename/move keeps modified; timestamps may truncate. §3.1.2 isSubscribed per user. Handlers do no permission checks (server/backend.rs:129); MemoryBackend enforces only maySetMetadata (memory.rs:1717). Direct HTTP Write and xattr: not implemented, nothing to do.
notes:
From batch 47: FileNode/set does not reject isSubscribed/shareWith on File/SymLink with invalidProperties (-19 §3.2.3); attempt broke filenode_copy_rejects_invalid_type_overrides via stored isSubscribed on source Directory - needs care. Base filenode-server does not reject destroy/rename/move of role Directories (chat layer enforces for chatspace root only). mayCreateTopLevelFileNode on move. Remaining -16 citations in filenode crates.
From batch 48: remaining stale citations: filenode-types src/backend.rs:63 (-16 §2), filenode-server filenode.rs NodeRole/NodeType and merge_filenode_overrides/create_type_error docs (-16), filenode_tests.rs header (-14).
2026-11-02 Mark: demoted from 'after 0.5.0' to 'only if someone uses it'. The reference backend does not need the full -19 ACL model to be useful; work this only when a real user needs permission enforcement.
2026-11-13 spec-sync batch 1: filenode-20 group NOT integrated (verify failed at b9e88191, branch worktree-wf_d9b28b7b-50b-9 kept unmerged). Remaining (blocking): onExists replace in FileNode/set and FileNode/copy returns nodeHasChildren (and may cascade-destroy with onDestroyRemoveChildren) before any discoverable/mayDelete check; -20 §3.2.3 orders discoverable, mayDelete, then nodeHasChildren. MemoryBackend per-user ACLs still absent. Do not close as superseded.
2026-11-13 filenode-20 integration (on main): 03fa5dec implements the onExists replace check order (discoverable, then mayDelete, then nodeHasChildren / forbidden for an undiscoverable descendant), shared by FileNode/set and FileNode/copy via replace_existing. Role rules and subtree change reporting landed under JMAP-3kbu (72f181a4, bda149e4). Still open here: (1) MemoryBackend has no per-user ACLs or principal_id enforcement and does not report newly undiscoverable nodes as destroyed (demoted: only if someone uses it). (2) Update path has no sibling-name collision check: -20 §3.2.3 applies onExists to create or update, and §3.1.1 forbids duplicate sibling names, but an update renaming/moving onto an existing sibling name succeeds and leaves two siblings named alike (follow-up bead to be filed). (3) Same FileNode/set does not check name uniqueness against the combined result of creates, updates and destroys (-19/-20 §3.2.3): destroy [x] plus create {name: same} in one call gives alreadyExists while x is still destroyed (same follow-up). (4) -20 §5: the plain FileNode/set onDestroyRemoveChildren cascade and the onSuccessDestroyOriginal cascade do not do replace_existing's undiscoverable-descendant check, so they can partially destroy a subtree; reuse that check. (5) jmap-chat-filenode-server check_space_destroy claims to cover the onExists replace, but replace_existing checks only files_rights.mayDelete (manage_channels for a Space root) while destroying the root needs manage_space, so a manage_channels member's replace/destroy with onDestroyRemoveChildren removes the descendants before the root destroy is refused: non-atomic, no escalation; document or ask the backend before cascading. Keep open; not superseded.
2026-11-13: items (2)-(3) (update-path collision / whole-/set uniqueness) are tracked by JMAP-6xas; items (4)-(5) (cascade undiscoverable-descendant check, check_space_destroy rights) by JMAP-uro2. This bead stays open only for (1): per-user ACLs / principal_id enforcement in MemoryBackend (Mark: only if someone uses it).
